title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Pages 205-208 study fppf sheaves on Sch/S of line bundles with extra structure on a family f: X -> S. P^c_{X/S} is the sheaf of line bundles with a connection. P^{ci}_{X/S} is the subsheaf of those with integrable connection. Here P^{cip}_{X/S} is the further subsheaf where the p-curvature also vanishes. The previous page gives two exact sequences. (2.1) is 0 -> P^{ci} -> P^c -> f_*(Z^2), the last map being curvature. (2.2) is 0 -> f_*Z^1 / dlog f_*O^* -> P^{ci} -> Pic -> R^2 f_*(Omega^{>=1}). In the favourable case Pic^0 = B is an abelian scheme with dual A^0 = Alb^0, and X -> A^1 (the Albanese torsor) induces f_*Omega^1_X = g_*Omega^1_{A^1}. Then P^{ci,0} is an extension of B by a vector bundle, identified with the universal vector extension of B.

This page, section 2 (continuation). Claim: the line bundles with connection pulled back along u, and in fact all of P^{c0}, already have curvature 0, i.e. land in P^{ci}. Two hypotheses are needed.
(2.4) f_*Omega^1_{X/S} = f_*Z^1_{X/S}: every relative global 1-form is closed, i.e. d: f_*Omega^1 -> f_*Omega^2 is zero. Grothendieck warns that f_*Z^1 is formed in fppf sheaves as Ker(f_*Omega^1 -> f_*Omega^2).
(2.5) V = f_*Omega^2_{X/S} is representable by a quasi-coherent module, i.e. it is a vector group.
Proof. The curvature map P^{c0} -> V is a homomorphism of S-group sheaves. P^{c0} is an extension of B (abelian scheme) by the vector part f_*Omega^1 / dlog. Since Hom(B, V) = 0 (a proper abelian scheme has no nonzero homomorphism to a vector group), the map is determined by its restriction to the vector part. On (f_*Omega^1)/dlog the curvature map is induced by d: f_*Omega^1 -> f_*Omega^2, which vanishes by (2.4). Hence (2.6): P^{c0} is contained in P^{ci}, i.e. P^{c0} = P^{ci0}. On the identity component every connection is automatically integrable. This is the mechanism that makes the 'space of line bundles in Pic^0 with connection' equal to the universal vector extension E(B).

Section 3. Assume p.1_S = 0. Define P^{cip} inside P^{ci}: integrable connections 'compatible with p-th powers', i.e. with zero p-curvature. When X/S has locally a p-base there is an exact sequence (3.1): 0 -> P^{cip} -> P^{ci} -> f_*(Omega^{1 (x) p}). The last map, K, is the p-curvature of a rank-one integrable connection, viewed as an additive map of group sheaves. Its target is the Frobenius-twisted 1-forms.
- The next page makes this explicit on the trivial bundle: for d + omega with omega closed, K_0(omega) = omega^{(x)p} - F^*(C omega), where C is the Cartier operation. K_0 is additive, the sum of a p-linear and a linear map.
- The next page also identifies P^{cip} with Pic of the Frobenius-twisted ringed space (X^{(p/S)}, O_S[O_X^p]), via Cartier descent.

Purpose. The goal is to understand Pic^natural (rank-one de Rham / crystalline Picard) and its relation to the universal extension and Dieudonné theory. In characteristic p the extra invariant is p-curvature, with the Cartier operator measuring the defect.
errors: (2.4) is a genuine restriction in characteristic p. Global 1-forms need not be closed (Mumford-type surfaces), and the Hodge-to-de Rham degeneration that guarantees (2.4) in characteristic 0 can fail. Grothendieck correctly lists it as a hypothesis rather than a fact.

The conclusion (2.6) concerns only the identity component P^{c0}, mapping onto B = Pic^0. Grothendieck tacitly uses that P^{c0} is an extension of an abelian scheme by a vector group. One also needs every line bundle in Pic^0 to admit a connection (vanishing Atiyah class). This follows by the same Hom(abelian scheme, vector group) = 0 argument applied to R^1 f_*Omega^1, but it is not stated.

The target of the p-curvature map is written Omega^{1 (x) p}. Correctly it is the Frobenius pullback F^*Omega^1 (equivalently Omega^1 of X^{(p)} pulled back), not literally the p-th tensor power. The map is p-linear, so the notation is suggestive rather than exact.
Exactness of (3.1) on the right is not claimed; the next page's (3.2) shows the cokernel involves the Cartier-type obstruction. Only left exactness is asserted on this page.

ideas.what: On the identity component, every connection on a line bundle (for Pic^0 an abelian scheme) is integrable, by Hom(abelian scheme, vector group) = 0 plus closedness of global 1-forms.
ideas.modern_name: Pic^natural,0 = universal vector extension E(Pic^0); automatic integrability of connections on Pic^0
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mazur-Messing (LNM 370, 1974); Messing; folklore going back to Rosenlicht/Serre for curves
ideas.where_published: Related material in Grothendieck, 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (Montréal 1970), on the universal extension; exact statement unsure

ideas.what: Exact sequence 0 -> (line bundles with connection of p-curvature 0) -> (line bundles with integrable connection) -> Frobenius-twisted 1-forms, via p-curvature.
ideas.modern_name: p-curvature map Pic^natural(X) -> H^0(X', Omega^1_{X'}) with kernel Pic(X') (Cartier descent); rank-one 'Hitchin map' of p-curvature
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz (Nilpotent connections, IHES 1970) for p-curvature and Cartier descent; Bezrukavnikov-Braverman (2007) and Laszlo-Pauly for the rank-one Hitchin-type use

ideas.what: Formula K_0(omega) = omega^p - F^*(C omega) for the p-curvature of d + omega, as an additive map that is p-linear plus linear (next page).
ideas.modern_name: Katz's formula for the p-curvature of a rank-one connection in terms of the Cartier operator

ideas.what: Defining sheaf-theoretic subfunctors P^c, P^{ci}, P^{cip} of the Picard functor, with fppf-sheaf caveats on forming f_*Z^1.
ideas.modern_name: Moduli of rank-one (flat) connections / de Rham Picard stack

missed.claim: Around 1972 Grothendieck sets up, in the relative fppf setting, the rank-one p-curvature map from line bundles with integrable connection to Frobenius-twisted 1-forms, with kernel the Picard functor of the Frobenius twist. This is the structure later exploited for nonabelian Hodge theory and geometric Langlands in characteristic p. There, Pic^natural is fibred over H^0(X', Omega^1) by p-curvature, with fibre over 0 equal to Pic(X'). The idea is known (Katz, Bezrukavnikov-Braverman) but this early, systematic group-sheaf formulation alongside the universal extension does not appear in Grothendieck's published texts.
missed.quote: (3.1) 0 -> P^{cip}_{X/S} -> P^{ci}_{X/S} --K p-courbure--> f_*(Omega^{1(x)p}_{X/S})  ... p-courbure = obstruction à la comp. aux puiss. p-ièmes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly historical: it shows the p-curvature/Cartier picture of Pic^natural was in Grothendieck's hands before Katz's and Mazur-Messing's publications. It offers little that is mathematically new.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct and coherent, but the content (automatic integrability on Pic^0 via Hom(B, vector group) = 0, the universal extension, the rank-one p-curvature sequence) is all in Mazur-Messing and Katz. Only the early date and relative fppf formulation are of historical interest.
transcription_corrections: Superscripts read as 'dR' on f_* are most likely 'fl' (fppf/flat topology pushforward), consistent with the next page's f^{fl}_*.
'(2.5) f_*^{dR} V = f_*(Omega^2) est compréhensible par un module' is more likely 'V = f_*^{fl}(Omega^2_{X/S}) est représentable par un module quasi-cohérent' (representable by a vector group).
'qui se rapporte nulle' is likely 'qui est supposée nulle' (referring to d: f_*Omega^1 -> f_*Omega^2 being zero).
'sous les conditions favorables (2.2)' may refer to the favourable case of the previous page ('Cas particulier'), not to the sequence (2.2) itself.
'(P^{c0}) ⊂ P^{ci}, i.e. P^{c0} = P^{ci0}' is confirmed.
